name: Alirocumab
route_note: subcutaneous injection every 2 weeks or every 4 weeks

discovery.note: A fully human IgG1 antibody co-developed with Sanofi. Year of first patent filing (priority December 2008, Regeneron, US 8,062,640).

tagline: First PCSK9 antibody approved by the FDA, central to a Supreme Court patent case
summary: Alirocumab is a fully human monoclonal antibody that inhibits PCSK9, increasing LDL receptor recycling and lowering LDL cholesterol by about 45–60%. The ODYSSEY OUTCOMES trial showed it reduced cardiovascular events and deaths after acute coronary syndrome.
mechanism: Alirocumab binds free PCSK9 in the circulation and stops it from attaching to hepatocyte LDL receptors, which would otherwise be degraded in lysosomes.
With more LDL receptors on the liver surface, clearance of LDL particles rises. Lipoprotein(a) also falls modestly.
uses: Reduction of cardiovascular events in established cardiovascular disease
Primary hyperlipidaemia including heterozygous familial hypercholesterolaemia

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: Approved in July, a month before evolocumab, as the first PCSK9 inhibitor in the US.

history.title: EU approval
history.detail: Approved by the European Commission in September.

history.title: ODYSSEY OUTCOMES
history.detail: Alirocumab reduces major cardiovascular events after ACS, with lower all-cause mortality.

history.title: Rights restructured
history.detail: Regeneron takes full US rights; Sanofi takes rights outside the US.

history.title: Amgen v. Sanofi
history.detail: The US Supreme Court rules Amgen's broad PCSK9 antibody patent claims invalid for lack of enablement.

pk.excretion: Not renally excreted as intact antibody

facts: The 2023 Amgen v. Sanofi ruling is a landmark decision on the enablement requirement for genus claims in biotechnology patents.

references.title: Schwartz GG et al. Alirocumab and cardiovascular outcomes after acute coronary syndrome (ODYSSEY OUTCOMES). N Engl J Med 2018
